stem.text: **FIGURE 5** shows a toy car moving in anticlockwise direction at a constant speed of \(3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) inside a vertical track with a \(50\ \mathrm{cm}\) diameter. The mass of the toy car is \(250\ \mathrm{g}\). Assuming that the toy car is always in contact with the track, calculate the

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: normal force when the toy car is at the top **AND** at the bottom of the track.

answer_scheme.heading: Answer scheme with step-by-step student hints
answer_scheme.radial_force_convention: Take the direction toward the centre of the circular track as positive.
answer_scheme.figure_reference_instruction: Refer to the original free-body diagrams beside the force equations.

steps.title: Determine the centripetal force
steps.student_hint: Convert mass and diameter to SI units first. The radius is half the diameter; then use F_c = mv²/r.

steps.title: At the top: resolve forces toward the centre
steps.student_hint: The centre of the circle is downward at the top. From the extracted FBD, both N and W = mg act toward the centre.

steps.title: Calculate the normal force at the top
steps.student_hint: Subtract the weight from the centripetal-force magnitude.

steps.title: At the bottom: resolve forces toward the centre
steps.student_hint: The centre is upward at the bottom. The original FBD shows N upward and W = mg downward. Thus their net upward force provides F_c.

steps.title: Calculate the normal force at the bottom
steps.student_hint: Add the weight to the centripetal-force magnitude.
